Wyszonki Koscielne Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wyszonki Kościelne, Poland

Demolished. Wyszonki Kościelne, a noble village belonging first to the Jałbrzyk family and later the Wyszyński family, saw its earliest documented Jewish community in 1674, confirmed present by 1735 and initially under the jurisdiction of the Tykocin kehillah, documented elsewhere in this collection. The Jewish population reached 177 (63 percent) by 1921; in 1937, antisemitic riots broke out, during which Antoni Czajkowski died and was later portrayed as a national hero by the right-wing National Party. Following the 1941 German occupation, Jews from Wyszonki Kościelne were sent to the ghetto in Wysokie Mazowieckie and deported to Treblinka. This cemetery was likely established at the end of the first half of the 18th century, remaining in use until WWII.
